claims.text: A2A v1 discovery uses /.well-known/agent-card.json and AgentCard.supportedInterfaces; protocolVersion belongs on each interface, not the card root.
A2A v1 JSON-RPC operation names are PascalCase, including SendMessage, SendStreamingMessage, GetTask, ListTasks, CancelTask, and SubscribeToTask.
JSON-RPC streaming uses Server-Sent Events and the v1 task/message/artifact model, not a Promise-only response with bespoke artifact fields.
Agent Cards declare authentication schemes, while credentials travel through standard HTTP mechanisms and must not be embedded as card secrets.
Authorization must scope task visibility and must not reveal whether an inaccessible resource exists; Prometheus must enforce its graph policy before mutation.
The current package is not an A2A v1 implementation despite its comments and description: it uses the old discovery path, bespoke card fields, slash-style methods, no ListTasks, and no streaming.
A2A supports URI-identified extensions and structured data parts; an A2UI adapter must negotiate and label its exact extension/version contract.
The stable dependency baseline is @a2a-js/sdk@1.0.1 for the A2A v1 family, pinned for this newly stable integration.

The official JavaScript server SDK provides the protocol model, request handler, task store, executor contract, JSON-RPC transport, and streaming event bus; Prometheus should adapt these instead of maintaining a second wire implementation.

The official TCK can grade normative scenarios across bindings and emit machine reports, but a Prometheus JSON-RPC-only result must not be presented as REST, gRPC, push, signing, or multi-tenant certification.

Prometheus targets A2UI v0.9.1, while the currently published dedicated A2UI-for-A2A extension page is explicitly v0.8 legacy; this version mismatch requires an honest adapter contract rather than a conformance claim for an unpublished v0.9 extension.
Legacy slash-style methods and bespoke graph parts may be retained only behind an explicitly named compatibility adapter with migration documentation, not on the v1 public surface.
